clue.text: The home team's let off at the outset

parts.note: to let off a gun is to fire it, and this piece comes at the outset
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A football team is given a reprieve right at the start of a home match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outset' puts FIRE first, before SIDE. 'The home' is defined by the hearth where the household gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth area stands, by metonymy, for domestic life and the household.

clue.text: Perfect angle's adopted at the crease

indicators.note: the fishing word takes in the batting word, as a family adopts a child

parts.note: to angle is to fish
a cricket batsman at the crease is in, batting

explanation.surface: A cricketer has found the ideal angle while standing at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter stands at the crease, so 'at the crease' means IN; 'adopted' puts it inside FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To perfect something is to give it its final polish or completion.

clue.text: Preservationists plugging bona fide property for hire

indicators.note: the trust's letters fill a gap inside the genuine word, as a plug fills a hole

parts.note: bona fide means genuine, real
NT is the National Trust, the British body that preserves historic buildings

explanation.surface: Heritage campaigners are promoting a genuine house that is up for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that preserves country houses and coastline; 'plugging' puts NT inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something let out for a fee, such as a flat or car, is a hired item.

clue.text: Dubious over greeting Japanese dish

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: sus is slang for suspicious, dubious
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: Someone is suspicious about being greeted with a Japanese meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works because this is a down clue: SUS stands above HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegared rice with raw fish is a classic food of Japan.

clue.text: Suitable animated serial to divide into autonomous sections

parts.note: decent means suitable, acceptable

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving, so the letters of serial are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: An appropriate cartoon series is to be split into self-governing parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' rearranges SERIAL into RALISE, placed after DECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To devolve power from the centre to regional bodies is to break an organisation into self-run units.

clue.text: Please turn over, sister, it's drooping

parts.note: PTO is the standard abbreviation printed at the foot of a page

explanation.surface: A note asks the reader to turn the page and tells a sister something is sagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's drooping' describes the medical condition rather than an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term names a sagging of the upper eyelid.

clue.text: Asian declines last of coffee from Republic of China …

parts.note: the Tai are a group of peoples of South-East Asia
to wane is to decline

indicators.note: only the final letter of coffee is taken

explanation.surface: An Asian traveller turns down the dregs of coffee from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian' looks like the definition, but it gives TAI; the definition is the end, Taiwan being officially the Republic of China. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is officially styled the Republic of China, so an adjective of origin from there fits.

clue.text: … to snatch another's port

definitions.meaning: to kidnap someone, originally to press men into service as sailors
a great harbour city of the other China, the People's Republic

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors were once drugged and abducted for crews bound for the Chinese city, giving a verb for kidnapping; the city itself is a major mainland seaport.

clue.text: Note I'm a con, possibly iffy icon is a source of money for me

definitions.text: iffy icon is a source of money for me

parts.note: si is a variant of ti, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of I'm a con may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A dodgy character confesses to being a fraud who profits from a dubious religious image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IMACON to MONIAC after SI. The definition describes someone who makes money from sacred things.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the buying or selling of church offices or sacred things, so its practitioner profits from holy objects.

clue.text: Service hospital is without equal

parts.note: nones is a church service said at the ninth hour
UCH is University College Hospital in London

explanation.surface: Care received at a hospital is said to be unrivalled.
explanation.walkthrough: UCH is University College Hospital, London; NONES is a monastic office said in mid-afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a person or thing that has no rival or match.

clue.text: Take to charming girl's limb

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, here with its possessive
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to start flattering a young woman's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive of Di gives DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone over and allay their hostility is to charm them.

clue.text: Mechanic's fat butt

parts.note: grease is animal fat
to make a monkey of someone is to make them the butt of a joke

explanation.surface: A mechanic's backside is chubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' is read as a target of ridicule, not a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang term for someone who repairs engines.

clue.text: Perhaps Paddington Bear's missing odd letters: he'll supply a new label

parts.note: Paddington is a London railway terminus, a station

indicators.note: the first and third letters of bear are dropped, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: Paddington Bear has lost his luggage tag and needs a new label.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a London railway terminus as well as the bear; dropping odd letters of BEAR leaves ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling paper goods supplies tags and stickers.

clue.text: Noble gas could make you groan

indicators.note: the letters could make a different word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A gas so inert it might make you moan.
explanation.definitionFit: An inert element of group 18 of the periodic table.

clue.text: Western state following Spain's lead in radio communications range

indicators.note: the state comes after the radio code word

parts.note: the first letter of Spain is S, which is Sierra in the NATO radio alphabet
Nevada is a western US state

explanation.surface: A Western state picks up Spanish radio messages from a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' places NEVADA after SIERRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of mountains in California, and another in Spain.

clue.text: Irish girl boy needled

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An Irish girl was annoyed by a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be annoyed or provoked.

clue.text: Union's unpopular court order

indicators.note: in means popular, and un- strips that word away

parts.note: an injunction is a court order

explanation.surface: A trade union's court order proves unpopular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpopular' read as un-popular removes IN (popular) from INJUNCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A joining point, such as where roads or wires meet.

clue.text: Boosts salary increase in good times

indicators.note: the pay rise sits inside the good times

parts.note: ups, as in ups and downs, are good times
a raise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: Getting a pay rise in prosperous times lifts spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RAISE inside UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift or elevate something is to give it a boost.

clue.text: 9 peacekeepers ran side by side

parts.note: UN peacekeepers belong to the United Nations
to parallel is to run alongside

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers ran alongside each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 9 across, a thing without equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no match or equal, as in the cross-referenced entry.

clue.text: Arnie's about to come in for Terminator's second bruising treatment

indicators.note: one piece replaces another, coming in for it

parts.note: Arnie is taken as written, Arnold Schwarzenegger's nickname

indicators.note: the second letter of Terminator is picked

parts.note: ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Arnold Schwarzenegger is about to arrive for the second Terminator film.
explanation.walkthrough: Schwarzenegger starred in the Terminator films. CA replaces the E, the second letter of Terminator.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal remedy from a mountain plant applied to bruises.

clue.text: No longer fresh bowler possibly over-used

parts.note: old means no longer fresh
a bowler is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler, past his best, has been played too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket but is the hard felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hackneyed or stale through repetition.

clue.text: Armada's beginning to travel west along shore of Spain for that of England

indicators.note: west is leftward in an across clue, so the letter moves towards the front

parts.note: costa is Spanish for ..., as in Costa del Sol

indicators.note: the first letter of Armada is taken

explanation.surface: The Spanish Armada sets off westwards along the Spanish shoreline towards England.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of COSTA travels west (leftwards) one place. 'that of England' means England's shore, using the English word.
explanation.definitionFit: The English word for the seaside edge of land.

clue.text: Reprobate cur led son astray

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dog led a boy off the right path.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or villain.

clue.text: Sauce bottle

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both cheeky impudence and boldness or courage.

clue.text: Correctly placed popular number discarded by U2 after its broadcast

indicators.note: the trimmed U comes after the scattered letters

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of its are spread out anew
the band name throws away its number

parts.note: the rock band's name, read as U followed by the word two
two is a number

explanation.surface: A hit single is dropped by the rock band U2 after it is aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns ITS into SIT; 'discarded by' takes the number 2 from U2, leaving U, which comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning in its original or proper position.

clue.text: Risks becoming involved with him in Brief Encounter

indicators.note: the letters get mixed up together, entangled

explanation.surface: He takes chances with a man in the classic film Brief Encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief Encounter is a 1945 British film, which steers away from the plain sense: a short clash.
explanation.definitionFit: A short fight or minor clash of forces.

clue.text: The game's up: my boss is half-cut in recession

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the whole run is read from the end

parts.note: the setter's boss is the editor, ED
half-cut and on both mean tipsy

explanation.surface: The setter says the editor is tipsy during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' reads EDISON backwards. In rugby, the referee's call ending the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby referee's call that signals the end of a match.

clue.text: Maybe brilliant players taking routine roles

parts.note: brilliant is a very small size of printing type
the cast are the players in a production

explanation.surface: Perhaps excellent actors are stuck playing the same parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Brilliant is an old name for a tiny type size, not praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors repeatedly given the same kind of part are stuck in a mould.
